newsitem.title: USA: Saab sees profits in 1998, expanded sales.
newsitem.headline: Saab sees profits in 1998, expanded sales.

text.p: Saab Automobile AB Chairman Robert Hendry said the Swedish automaker has set a goal of achieving profitability in 1998 and "acceptable returns" by the year 2000.

Hendry, speaking to reporters at Detroit's North American International Auto Show, said the goals were linked to plans by Saab to expand worldwide sales to 150,000 cars by the year 2000 from about 99,000 in 1996.

Hendry said a major part of the projected sales increase will come from the introduction of a new upscale car model that will replace the Saab 9000 in the United States. The new car, code-named 640, will be produced in Sweden and will be introduced later this year with a station wagon version to follow in early 1998.
However, Hendry said Saab will continue to produce the 9000 for European markets for another two to four years.

Saab also plans to introduce several high-performance versions of its mainstay 900 model in the next two years. The company may consider adding a third model line but Hendry said it would have to meet stringent financial and profit requirements.
"Any third car line is going to have to earn its own way," Hendry said.
Separately, GM Chairman Jack Smith told reporters at the auto show that he has confidence in Hendry's leadership of Saab, which is jointly owned by GM and Sweden's Investor AB.
"They're going to do well," Smith said of Saab. "I'm feeling pretty good about Saab and what he's going to do over there."
GM in the last year has injected an additional $500 million in capital into Saab in an effort to help the company reverse losses in recent years.
